Formal Specification of sort_list
=================================

Notation
--------
|L|            : length of list L
L[i]           : element of L at index i (0-based, defined for 0 <= i < |L|)
occ(x, L)      : number of occurrences of element x in L
                 occ(x, L) = |{ i : 0 <= i < |L| and L[i] = x }|
<=_Z           : the usual non-decreasing order on integers


First-Order Logic Formulation
-----------------------------

Predicate definitions:

  Sorted(M)  =def  forall i. (0 <= i < |M| - 1  ->  M[i] <= M[i+1])

  Perm(L, M) =def  forall x. (occ(x, L) = occ(x, M))

    (i.e., L and M have exactly the same elements with the same
     multiplicities -- multiset equality)

Main theorem (the specification):

  forall L.  Sorted(sort_list(L))  and  Perm(L, sort_list(L))

Equivalently, using a global-index sortedness condition
(provable to be equivalent to the adjacent-pair version for lists
over a total order):

  forall L.  ( forall i, j. (0 <= i <= j < |sort_list(L)|
                              ->  sort_list(L)[i] <= sort_list(L)[j]) )
             and
             ( forall x. occ(x, L) = occ(x, sort_list(L)) )


Proof-Assistant Formulation (Lean 4 style)
------------------------------------------

def Sorted (l : List Int) : Prop :=
  forall i j, 0 <= i -> i <= j -> j < l.length -> l[i]! <= l[j]!

def Perm (l m : List Int) : Prop :=
  forall x, l.count x = m.count x

theorem sort_list_spec (L : List Int) :
    Sorted (sort_list L) /\ Perm L (sort_list L)


Proof-Assistant Formulation (Coq style)
---------------------------------------

Definition Sorted (m : list Z) : Prop :=
  forall i j, i <= j -> j < length m -> nth i m 0 <=? nth j m 0 = true.

Definition Perm (l m : list Z) : Prop :=
  forall x, count_occ x l = count_occ x m.

Theorem sort_list_spec : forall L : list Z,
  Sorted (sort_list L) /\ Perm L (sort_list L).
